cards.sourceMeaning: Published interpretation square:saturn:sun: An established role can feel demanding when its obligations require more deliberate effort than usual. Saturn's square to the Sun highlights where expectations outpace available capacity, showing where a routine or responsibility needs clearer boundaries.
cards.meaning: An established responsibility can ask for more deliberate effort. Where its expectations exceed the capacity available, its boundary may need to become clearer.
sceneDetails: An extra check or another version added beside the original task.
One afternoon set aside for a familiar responsibility.
The same task moved into a later calendar opening without changing what it includes.
cards.practicalDistinction: Moving the task to a later opening may leave the extra check attached.
optionalDirections: If the original work already fills the afternoon, the extra check could be left out.
requiredConditions: The responsibility asking more effort is an interpretive possibility, not an established condition of the reader today.
Any actual mismatch between expectations and capacity must remain conditional.
Follow-up references to the task, added scope or boundary must remain inside the possible scene.
limitations: Do not add a recent onset, an actual overloaded afternoon, unsustainable effort or a known change in capacity.
Do not turn the optional boundary into a command to refuse work or a judgment about the reader's discipline.
Calendar and task details are authored benchmark illustrations, not calculation facts.

cards.sourceMeaning: Published natal lens, an interpretive possibility: Following more than one line of curiosity can help a direction take shape. If several possible projects compete for the same free afternoon, sampling a few and choosing one to pursue may be different stages.
cards.meaning: Several lines of curiosity may help a direction emerge. Exploring possible projects and choosing one to pursue can be separate stages.
sceneDetails: A page of notes for one idea beside a tab open for another.
One possible project kept as a note beside the project selected for the afternoon.
cards.practicalDistinction: Sampling a few projects and choosing one may be different stages.
optionalDirections: If several projects compete for that afternoon, a note can hold the second idea without promising it those hours.
requiredConditions: This natal lens is an interpretive possibility, not a fixed personality claim.
The multiple-project scene applies only if several possibilities are competing for the same time.
Keep the distinction between exploration and commitment visible in the shared project scene.
limitations: Do not call the reader distracted, indecisive, scattered or unable to finish.
Do not imply that all interests must become projects or that choosing one means abandoning the others.
The notes and tab are possible illustrations, not observed behavior.

cards.sourceMeaning: Published transit chapter: If an earlier way of handling this no longer fits, this return offers a chance to try a smaller adjustment to a method or boundary.
cards.meaning: If an earlier way of handling the responsibility no longer fits, this return offers a chance to try a smaller adjustment to a method or boundary.
sceneDetails: A task put into a different calendar opening while its contents stay the same.
A defined stopping point for what belongs inside this afternoon's commitment.
cards.practicalDistinction: Moving a task to a later slot does not change its size; adjusting what is included or where it stops can change the method or boundary.
optionalDirections: If the earlier method no longer fits, change one part of the task's method or boundary.
Make a stopping point visible before an extra check or version enters the agreement.
requiredConditions: Preserve the condition that an earlier way must no longer fit before offering an adjustment as a return-chapter application.
A calculated return does not establish that a life situation recurred or that a previous attempt failed.
Use any chronology only from A1 exactly, with C1 and I1 as parents.
limitations: Do not tell the reader they have been here before or have already failed with this method.
Do not turn a smaller adjustment into a recommendation for a wholesale restart.
Calendar, task-size and stopping-point details are authored benchmark illustrations.

cards.sourceMeaning: Published interpretation trine:jupiter:mars: Enthusiasm and practical initiative reinforce one another when an aim is well chosen. Jupiter's trine to Mars frames moments when effort encounters little friction, making it natural to take on a larger piece of work or pursue an emerging opening.
cards.meaning: When an aim is well chosen, enthusiasm and practical initiative can reinforce each other, making a larger piece of work or an emerging opening easier to take up.
sceneDetails: A page of notes beginning to become an outline.
Another piece of the same project starting to look appealing.
cards.practicalDistinction: A well-chosen aim can bring enthusiasm and a practical start together; ease in taking up a piece is not a guarantee about its result.
optionalDirections: Notice the moment an appealing next piece begins to look like something to take on.
requiredConditions: Preserve the well-chosen-aim condition; do not assert that the reader's current aim is well chosen.
Ease is an interpretive possibility, not a promise of success or an actual opportunity arriving.
limitations: Do not guarantee motivation, success, luck, a reward or an opportunity.
Do not turn initiative into an instruction to accept more work.
The notes, outline and appealing addition are authored benchmark illustrations.

cards.sourceMeaning: Published tension synthesis square:saturn:sun_tension_trine:jupiter:mars (parents: C1, I1, C2, I2): Giving a plan more scope can increase the structure needed to carry it. A task whose ambitions are growing beyond its agreed limits offers one place to notice that tension.
cards.meaning: Giving a plan more scope can increase the structure needed to carry it. A possible task growing beyond its agreed limits makes that tension visible.
sceneDetails: An appealing extra piece added to the same project.
One more check or another version enlarging the same proposed task.
cards.practicalDistinction: Ease in beginning more work is different from having enough structure to carry the expanded commitment.
optionalDirections: Notice whether an appealing addition changes the amount the original agreement includes.
Consider the structure a larger piece would need before adding it to the same agreement.
requiredConditions: Use only with C1, I1, C2 and I2; preserve both contact interpretations and the combined tension.
Added scope and limits being exceeded must remain possible, not assumed facts about the reader's project.
limitations: Do not imply all growth is overcommitment or that a larger plan must be refused.
Do not promise that a boundary will produce success or reduce strain.
The project, notes and proposed addition are authored benchmark illustrations.

principles.instruction: Lead with a supported visible detail or plain distinction; cut an abstract preface that announces the lesson.
Let one concrete consequence explain the distinction. Cut a following abstract sentence that repeats it.
Keep a source condition and its possibility word attached to their own claim. An immediate clear reference may continue the same hypothetical; repeat its condition only when needed for clarity.
Let a supported object or small optional choice finish the thought. Cut a counselor reminder, prescribed script or final recap that adds no meaning.
Shortening must preserve possibility and scope. Do not add speed, ease, frequency or necessity while making the prose more direct.
